root_cause.text: In the SCTP_SENDALL loop in `sctp_sendmsg()`, `list_for_each_entry_safe()` cached the next `ep->asocs` cursor in `tmp` but did not revalidate it after `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()` could drop the socket lock, so `tmp` could become stale and point to a freed or migrated association.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `tmp = list_next_entry(asoc, asocs);` after `iov_iter_revert()` and explains that `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()` may release the socket lock in `sctp_wait_for_sndbuf()`, during which another thread can peel off or free the association cached in `@tmp`; it also states that `sctp_wait_for_sndbuf()` only revalidates `@asoc`, not `@tmp`, leading to use-after-free or list-walk/type confusion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Recompute the SCTP association list cursor after lock drop to avoid using a stale iterator when associations may have changed.
intent_record.what: After reverting the I/O iterator on error, the code now reassigns the cached `tmp` cursor with `list_next_entry(asoc, asocs)` and adds a comment explaining why the cursor must be re-derived after `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()` may have dropped the socket lock.
intent_record.how: If `sctp_sendmsg_to_asoc()` temporarily releases the socket lock, the association list may change while waiting for send buffer space; this update refreshes the iteration cursor so later list traversal does not use a stale pointer and can continue safely after the lock is reacquired.
